limiterDetail: Wind is light to moderate (4.5–7.7 kt now, ECMWF day 6.8 kt, gusts 11) and rain light. The main limiter is current: it builds through the day, and by afternoon Tara, Turda, Decabaitot, Alava, Culion, Binudac and Barangonan run 1.0–1.8 kt. Wind then rises from about Thu 1 AM (10–14 kt on the Nangalao, Maglalambay, Panlaitan and Ciron side).

pagasa.detail: PAGASA: no gale, wind signal or heavy-rain warning for Calamian / MIMAROPA. Latest: Tropical Cyclone Warning, Super Typhoon Rosal (Champi), Signal #1 , Wed 21 Oct 4:52 AM PHT, for Batanes, Cagayan, Isabela, Apayao, Ilocos Norte and Catanduanes. Gale Warning No. 2 covers the northern and eastern seaboards of Luzon and the eastern seaboard of Visayas only. Strong to gale-force gusts are forecast for most of Luzon and Visayas Thu 22 and Fri 23. Rosal exits PAR by Sat 24.

changed.title: ⚠️ What changed since yesterday afternoon
items: The late-week outlook eased. Fri 23 is no longer the worst day: ECMWF cut it from 12 kt (gusts 18) to 10 kt (gusts 16), so it's back to MARGINAL. Sun 25's heavy rain is gone too (~18.8 mm down to ~5.7 mm, moderate). Thu 22 is again the single worst day (POOR, 11 kt, gusts 16, current 0.9 kt).

Supply: the tight stretch is now shorter. Arrivals still thin as Thursday's weak catch lands (BELOW NORMAL around Fri 23), but the "TIGHT through Tue 27" call is dropped; the weekend and early next week look NORMAL to softening rather than tight. Shortage risk stays ELEVATED (guide only), surge OFF.

Super Typhoon Rosal (Champi) is now 990 km east of Northern Luzon with Signal #1 widened to Batanes, Cagayan, Isabela, Apayao, Ilocos Norte and Catanduanes (PAGASA, 4:52 AM PHT). Still nothing for Palawan, and PAGASA lists our waters among "other coastal waters" under 2.0 m. But its strong-to-gale gust warning now covers most of Luzon and Visayas on both Thu 22 and Fri 23 , so exposed grounds could gust above the model.

shortageRisk: Surge flag OFF (unchanged). Shortage risk stays ELEVATED , but the tightest arrivals are now Thu 22 to Fri 23 instead of running to Tue 27. Tara, Turda and Decabaitot run BELOW NORMAL locally on current. Buying from this morning's landings is still the best move before Thursday–Friday thin out.

bestWindow.headline: This morning, about 6 AM to noon
details: 6–8 AM: Maglalambay and Panlaitan at 4–8 kt on 0.2 kt current (the model's best combined hour is 6 AM there), before their wind jumps to 10–12 kt from 8 AM.
6 AM–noon: Coron, Galoc and Linapacan on 5–9 kt and 0.1–0.3 kt current, the easiest all-round grounds; light showers (0.3–0.7 mm/h) reach the Coron side from about 9 AM.
Keep boats off Tara and Turda all day, and off Decabaitot and Alava after about 1 PM. Tonight wind builds to 10–14 kt after Thu 1 AM, so Thursday early trips will be rough.
